key_insight: A parameterized physics-informed neural network predicts embedded microfluidic cooling performance across a continuous geometric design space with reported computational savings exceeding four orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Fast thermohydraulic predictions could accelerate the design and optimization of embedded manifold microchannels for high-performance chip cooling.
method: Use four geometric dimensions and three spatial coordinates as network inputs.
Combine geometric ansatz embedding, SOAP optimization, and a thermal-conductivity-based learning curriculum.
Train with an optimized JAX backend on a single consumer-grade GPU.
evidence_signal: Against finite-element simulations, the abstract reports relative errors of 8.1% for velocity and 5.6% for temperature, with training convergence in under four hours.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish experimental validation or accuracy outside the evaluated geometric and operating ranges.
paper_title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
